summary: FD_TC_209_Travel Completed | APPR | PAL Airlines as MSL | Spotty Coding | DDS Behaviour Validation
title: Travel Completed | APPR | PAL Airlines as MSL | Spotty Coding | DDS Behaviour Validation
description:
Customer travels on an AC-ticketed itinerary where the disrupted leg is operated by PAL Airlines (interline partner). PAL is identified as the Most Significant Leg (MSL). PAL's disruption coding is known to be spotty/inconsistent � this test validates DDS behaviour in BOTH scenarios: (A) when PAL coding IS present and DDS can evaluate, and (B) when PAL coding is MISSING/incomplete and DDS cannot determine controllability. Confirms that when coding is absent, DDS correctly flags the case for agent review rather than auto-deciding. This is critical because spotty coding from PAL may result in missing disruption codes, missing delay reasons, or incomplete flight status data.

Prerequisites:
PNR: Single passenger (�lise Beaumont), multi-leg itinerary. Leg 1: AC 501 YUL?MNL (AC operated, no disruption). Leg 2: PAL 102 MNL?CEB (PAL operated, disrupted � 4hr delay). Itinerary: Leg 2 scheduled arrival 14:00, Actual arrival 18:00 (4hr delay). MSL: PAL 102 MNL?CEB (PAL is the operating carrier on the disrupted leg). Disruption code on PAL leg: TEST BOTH SCENARIOS � Scenario A: Code present (e.g., 42 equivalent); Scenario B: Code MISSING/NULL. Booking changes: None. Carrier: AC ticketing carrier, PAL operating carrier on disrupted leg. 72hrs: Elapsed. Time limit: Within 366 days. No duplicate case. CyberSource: GREEN.
